full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-petitioner's case, in short, is that he instituted OC Suit No. 169 of 1985 against the opposite parties praying for establishment of title and confirmation of possession contending, inter alia that the suit land was auction purchased by Haji Yunus Mollah with the ejmali fund of brothers and sisters. Thereafter the suit land along with other lands were partitioned amongst the co-sharers in terms of the Solenama filed in Title Suit No. 157 of 1957 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi and in accordance with the terms of the solenama the plaintiff got the suit land. It is also the case of the plaintiff that during RS Operation the suit land was recorded in the names of Haji Yunus Molla and the Government of Bangladesh which has clouded his own title and for removal of that cloud the plaintiff had to file the aforesaid suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. But during the proceeding of the Suit the plaintiff had to amend the plaint when the Advocate Commissioner found 2.35 acres of land out of the possession of the plaintiff. The plaintiff then by way of amendment prayed for recovery of khas possession of this land from defendant No. 14. 

 8. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of opposite party No. 14, submits that they got delivery of possession of 2.35 acres of land of the suit property from Haji Yunus Mollah and they constructed a School, a Mahila Madrassa and a Mosque over the same and they are enjoying the usufructs and the pleader Commissioner found their possession in the same which has been admitted by the plaintiff when he amended his plaint and prayed for recovery of khas possession of this portion of the land. The learned Advocate contends that as defendant No. 14 is in possession of the suit property on the basis of a gift for over 12 years and during that period when the plaintiff has not laid his claim over the same the suit is barred by limitation. The learned Advocate contends that there is no proof that after the Judgment in the partition suit the plaintiff got possession over the suit property and thereafter he was dispossessed either by Haji Yunus Mollah or by opposite party No. 14 and he brought this suit within 12 years from the date of dispossession. It has been also contended that though according to the plaintiff the partition suit was disposed of on 26.10.57 and though the record of right was published in 1983 the plaintiff has not come within 12 years from either years which made the suit barred by limitation. 

 9. The petitioner filed the aforesaid OC Suit No. 169 of 1985 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. Subsequently, he had to amend the plaint and sought recovery of khas possession from opposite Party No. 14 from 2.35 acres of land. His specific case is that the suit land was purchased by Haji Yunus Mollah with the ejmali fund of the brothers and sisters. Subsequently, Title Suit No. 157 of 1957 was filed for Partition and a solenama was filed and on the basis of the terms of the solenama the plaintiff got the suit land. As against this the defence case is that this plaintiff was merely a benamder of Haji Yunus Mollah who himself purchased the property with his own money but for keeping the property from being taken over by the Government he adopted a method by way of getting a suit filed for partition wherein a solenama was filed in which the land was shown to have been allotted to plaintiff though, as a matter of fact, the land continued to remain with Haji Yunus Mollah and as the plaintiff was the benamder, no step was taken by the parties in the suit for drawing up of a decree. 

 12. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title over 4.8525 decimals of land and also confirmation of possession. Initially defendant No. 14 was not a party in the suit. This defendant No. 14 was impleaded by the trial Court's order dated 28.3.88 and thereafter a commission was taken for tocal investigation and the Commissioner found defendant No. 14 in possession of 2.35 acres out of the suit land for which the plaintiff had to amend the plaint and prayed for recovery of khas possession of this portition of the suit land. In such circumstances, the plaintiff is required to prove that since the disposal of the partition suit or since purchase by Haji Yunus Mollah the plaintiff continued to possess the suit land till the filing of the suit on 29.9.85. The plaintiff before the trial Court examined 3 witnesses and also produced the order passed in the partition suit, rent receipts, copy of the return and khatian to prove his possession in addition to the oral evidence. It appears that the plaintiff himself was not examined but his son appeared as PW 1 in support of the claim of the plaintiff.
